purpose: Remediation effort estimates and family ranking metadata for Studio improvement guidance; does not change trust scoring.
review_basis: Manual inspection of current policy IDs, evaluator conditions and the seven-server independent_mcp_scores.json export. No effort measurements or remediation-success dataset; confidence values are subjective review estimates, not calibrated probabilities.

easy_score_scale.1: Very hard: major feature or architectural implementation, with several dependencies.
easy_score_scale.2: Hard: protocol, authentication, lifecycle or substantial feature integration.
easy_score_scale.3: Moderate: several coordinated changes or infrastructure/schema/storage work.
easy_score_scale.4: Easy: a focused handler, validation or configuration change in an existing feature.
easy_score_scale.5: Very easy: a localized truthful metadata or field update in an existing feature.

confidence_scale.meaning: Confidence in the portability of the easy_score estimate across implementations, not probability of passing and not trust-score confidence.

interpretation.0.9_to_1.0: Clear narrow evaluator condition with limited implementation uncertainty.
interpretation.0.75_to_0.89: Clear condition with some compatibility, integration or domain uncertainty.
interpretation.0.5_to_0.74: Architecture, external ownership or heuristic diagnosis makes effort substantially variable.
interpretation.below_0.5: Insufficient basis; obtain more evidence before using the estimate.

assumptions: The developer controls the server code or relevant configuration and can reassess after changes.
Estimates concern repairing existing intended features; implementing an absent optional feature requires a fresh effort estimate.
Descriptions, declarations and hints must reflect actual behavior; passing a presence check alone is not the objective.
Each rule belongs to one primary family to avoid counting its weight twice; dependencies can still cross families.
Family easy_score estimates the combined work for that family, not the sum of member easy scores. Re-estimate for the actual eligible subset.
Family membership identifies a shared remediation area, not a guarantee that one change passes every member. Singleton families are intentional.

ranking.family_priority: sum(distinct eligible member configured_weight) * family.easy_score * family.confidence
ranking.weight_source: Each rule.weight is a configured-weight snapshot from EXPERIMENTS/output/independent_mcp_scores.json at policy.definition (agentopia-mcp-v1 version 1.2.0). For ranking, read configured_weight from the current validated assessment or the exact matching policy definition; refresh these snapshots when that policy changes.
ranking.points_meaning: Potential configured points from eligible nonpassing rules, not a guarantee of points or a change to the trust-score formula.
ranking.zero_weight: Keep informational rules in the catalog, but zero-weight-only families do not qualify as point-gain tips.
ranking.current_scope: Studio selects up to five eligible families deterministically; DeepInfra generates guidance only. Applicable skipped checks support verification guidance without estimated points. Unknown checks are excluded from improvement tips and family ranking.

eligibility.failed: Candidate only when applicable, evidence-supported, and the family action addresses the actual recorded failure.
eligibility.skipped: Candidate only after the skip reason and prerequisites establish an intended, applicable, actionable opportunity. Do not infer a defect or award points from a skip.
eligibility.not_applicable: Exclude from ranking. Optional absence, an older revision, or a feature intentionally not declared is not automatically a recommended improvement.
eligibility.unknown: Exclude from improvement tips and family ranking. Insufficient evidence does not establish an actionable defect or potential point gain.
eligibility.passed: Exclude from potential gain; retain only as dependency/context if needed.
eligibility.blocked_checks: Resolve prerequisites first and reassess. Do not count newly enabled downstream checks as guaranteed passes.
eligibility.skip_caution: Current evaluators frequently mark skipped checks not_applicable; do not override that label through a generic rule-family default.

families.name: Server identity and instructions
families.easy_reason: Populate a few existing initialization response fields without adding a new subsystem.
families.confidence_reason: Checks directly test nonblank strings; authoring accurate instructions still needs server knowledge.
families.shared_work: Edit the serverInfo and instructions response builder. Each field remains a separate requirement.
families.eligibility_note: A usable initialization or metadata response must already exist.

rules.name: Server name present
rules.easy_reason: Add the real server name to serverInfo.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator only checks a nonblank name; the response location is explicit.

rules.name: Server version present
rules.easy_reason: Supply the deployed server version in serverInfo.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator only checks a nonblank version; release automation may need wiring.

rules.name: Instructions present
rules.easy_reason: Add concise, truthful server usage instructions.
rules.confidence_reason: The string check is clear; writing useful instructions requires domain knowledge.

families.name: Supported protocol versions
families.easy_reason: Align negotiation and discovery, and implement compatibility before advertising a newer revision.
families.confidence_reason: Some failures are configuration mismatches; actual revision upgrades can require substantial SDK changes.
families.shared_work: Maintain one truthful supported-version registry used by negotiation and discovery. Passing one version check does not prove the others.
families.eligibility_note: Respect actual implemented revisions; do not advertise unsupported features to gain points.

rules.name: Recognized protocol revision
rules.easy_reason: Negotiate an actually supported recognized revision, possibly through an SDK update.
rules.confidence_reason: The accepted registry is clear; compatibility effort depends on the server implementation.

rules.name: Latest protocol support
rules.easy_reason: Implement the target revision before advertising it in discovery.
rules.confidence_reason: This can be a substantial protocol upgrade rather than a version-string edit.

rules.name: Discovery includes negotiated revision
rules.easy_reason: Generate negotiation and discovery versions from the same supported-version registry.
rules.confidence_reason: The equality relationship is explicit; both protocol paths must already work.

rules.name: Supported versions
rules.easy_reason: Return a nonempty list of supported revision strings from discovery.
rules.confidence_reason: The list validation is direct; each advertised revision must be genuinely supported.

families.name: Capability declarations and usable listings
families.easy_reason: Align declared features with their real listing handlers and complete catalog results.
families.confidence_reason: The correction may be a declaration edit, a handler repair, or a pagination fix.
families.shared_work: Use a consistent catalog registry for capability declarations and listings; tool, prompt and resource handlers can still need separate repairs.
families.eligibility_note: Do not add optional tools, prompts or resources solely because their absence was skipped.

rules.name: Tools declaration matches listing
rules.easy_reason: Make the tools declaration match a working, complete tools/list response.
rules.confidence_reason: A declaration mismatch is small; missing handlers or broken pagination cost more.

rules.name: Prompts declaration matches listing
rules.easy_reason: Make the prompts declaration match a working, complete prompts/list response.
rules.confidence_reason: The same check can fail from either metadata or listing behavior.

rules.name: Resources declaration matches listing
rules.easy_reason: Make the resources declaration match a working, complete resources/list response.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator exposes the mismatch, but catalog implementation complexity varies.

rules.name: tools at least one
rules.easy_reason: If tools are intended, provide at least one real usable tool in the declared catalog.
rules.confidence_reason: Creating meaningful tool behavior can be much harder than adding a list entry.

families.name: HTTP transport and GET behavior
families.easy_reason: Repair the HTTP adapter and applicable stream handling; this can touch framework and proxy configuration.
families.confidence_reason: A compatible SDK can simplify the work, but transport failures have several infrastructure causes.
families.shared_work: Review HTTP routing and transport integration together. GET may correctly return HTTP 405 without implementing a stream.
families.eligibility_note: Apply the transport contract for the observed revision; do not introduce unsupported streaming features.

rules.name: Streamable HTTP transport
rules.easy_reason: Implement a working supported HTTP exchange through the server transport adapter.
rules.confidence_reason: Framework, proxy and SDK behavior determine how much integration work is needed.

rules.name: Legacy GET stream contract
rules.easy_reason: Return an appropriate SSE response or explicitly reject GET with HTTP 405.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator accepts two clear paths; existing clients may constrain the choice.

families.name: Notification response handling
families.easy_reason: Correct the notification handler response status and empty body.
families.confidence_reason: The evaluator has a narrow response contract, although middleware may append a body.
families.shared_work: Adjust the notification response branch and verify middleware preserves it.
families.eligibility_note: Requires the applicable notification exchange to be observable.

rules.name: Notification accepted correctly
rules.easy_reason: Return HTTP 202 with exactly zero body bytes for the tested notification.
rules.confidence_reason: The required response is explicit and usually localized to one handler.

families.name: Legacy session deletion
families.easy_reason: Handle DELETE consistently with the server session design and verify follow-up behavior.
families.confidence_reason: Declining deletion can be simple; invalidating sessions correctly requires lifecycle work.
families.shared_work: Review the legacy DELETE handler and session store together; HTTP 405 is an accepted explicit refusal.
families.eligibility_note: No issued session or an expired session is not automatically a defect or an easy-point opportunity.

rules.name: Legacy session deletion contract
rules.easy_reason: Explicitly decline deletion with HTTP 405 or invalidate an accepted deletion and reject the old session.
rules.confidence_reason: Alternative valid behaviors exist; session-store ownership determines effort.

families.name: Error response construction
families.easy_reason: Repair request dispatch and error serialization while retaining the correct condition-specific responses.
families.confidence_reason: Expected responses are explicit, but different error branches may have separate owners.
families.shared_work: Centralize error construction where useful; malformed requests, unknown methods and unsupported revisions remain distinct cases.
families.eligibility_note: Use each rule expectation and revision; do not return one error code for all failures.

rules.name: Invalid request rejected
rules.easy_reason: Reject the malformed numeric-method request through request validation.
rules.confidence_reason: The probe is specific; middleware or dispatch changes are usually focused.

rules.name: Invalid request diagnostic code
rules.easy_reason: Return the expected diagnostic code for the observed invalid-request case.
rules.confidence_reason: A code mapping is often localized, but the failure must first be classified correctly.

rules.name: Unknown method error
rules.easy_reason: Return the expected JSON-RPC code and HTTP status for an unknown method.
rules.confidence_reason: Both expected values and the tested dispatch branch are explicit.

rules.name: Unsupported version error
rules.easy_reason: Reject unsupported revisions with the required error data listing supported and requested revisions.
rules.confidence_reason: This needs coordinated version validation and structured error data.

families.name: Tool identifiers
families.easy_reason: Repair tool names and their registry entries while preserving existing client mappings.
families.confidence_reason: Name checks are simple; renaming public tools can require compatibility changes.
families.shared_work: Use a validated tool registry to ensure nonblank, valid and unique names; one rename can affect several checks.
families.eligibility_note: Only relevant to existing or intended tool catalogs.

rules.name: tools name present in all
rules.easy_reason: Add a nonblank name to each existing tool entry.
rules.confidence_reason: The required field is explicit; dispatch must use the same name.

rules.name: tools names unique
rules.easy_reason: Assign distinct names and update the corresponding dispatch mappings.
rules.confidence_reason: Duplicate detection is direct, but renames can affect clients.

rules.name: tools names valid format
rules.easy_reason: Replace invalid characters or lengths and update references to renamed tools.
rules.confidence_reason: The naming pattern is explicit; client compatibility adds uncertainty.

families.name: Tool and input documentation
families.easy_reason: Write accurate descriptions for existing tools and their directly reachable input fields.
families.confidence_reason: These are localized metadata edits; useful wording still requires knowledge of the tool.
families.shared_work: Update the tool-definition source used to generate descriptions and input schemas; tool and field descriptions are independent fields.
families.eligibility_note: Do not fabricate inputs or tool behavior just to satisfy nonblank checks.

rules.name: tools description present in all
rules.easy_reason: Add truthful, nonblank descriptions to existing tools.
rules.confidence_reason: The check tests presence rather than prose quality; domain review remains necessary.

rules.name: tools input properties documented
rules.easy_reason: Add descriptions to the actual input properties checked by the schema walker.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator identifies the structural scope; schemas with many fields require more editing.

families.name: Tool input schemas
families.easy_reason: Correct schema structure while preserving accepted inputs and actual tool behavior.
families.confidence_reason: Syntax faults are easy; references, unions and generated schemas can be more involved.
families.shared_work: Repair the input-schema generator and validate its output against the supported dialect.
families.eligibility_note: Requires actual tools; an unsupported dialect or incomplete observation is not automatically an invalid schema.

rules.name: tools input schema valid
rules.easy_reason: Correct invalid JSON Schema and the applicable input object structure.
rules.confidence_reason: Structural expectations are explicit, but fixes can change tool input compatibility.

families.name: Tool output schemas
families.easy_reason: Repair declared output schemas and any applicable legacy root-object restriction.
families.confidence_reason: Both checks inspect schema declarations, but applicability differs by protocol revision.
families.shared_work: Validate the same output-schema definitions for general syntax and applicable root structure; one schema edit may address both.
families.eligibility_note: Optional absent output schemas and inapplicable legacy restrictions should stay skipped.

rules.name: tools output schema valid
rules.easy_reason: Repair an existing declared output schema to match a supported schema dialect.
rules.confidence_reason: Schema complexity and the real output contract determine effort.

rules.name: tools output schema root object
rules.easy_reason: Use an object root when the observed legacy revision requires it.
rules.confidence_reason: The structural condition is explicit, but changing the public output contract needs care.

families.name: Truthful tool behavior hints
families.easy_reason: Set behavior hints consistently with the actual operation rather than merely changing labels.
families.confidence_reason: Metadata edits are small, but the evaluator uses heuristics and does not execute tools.
families.shared_work: Review annotations in one tool-definition pass; presence, destructive intent and contradictions are separate checks.
families.eligibility_note: Confirm real tool semantics before assigning read-only or destructive hints.

rules.name: tools annotations present
rules.easy_reason: Declare meaningful boolean behavior hints for each existing tool.
rules.confidence_reason: The field checks are explicit; choosing truthful values requires domain knowledge.

rules.name: tools annotations destructive declared
rules.easy_reason: Align destructive-operation hints with the actual tool behavior.
rules.confidence_reason: Delete intent is inferred heuristically from names and descriptions; inspection is necessary.

rules.name: tools annotations hints consistent
rules.easy_reason: Remove contradictory read-only and destructive declarations using the true behavior.
rules.confidence_reason: The boolean contradiction is direct, but the correct replacement needs semantic review.

families.name: Task execution capability alignment
families.easy_reason: Align task-support declarations with a genuinely implemented task capability.
families.confidence_reason: This may require task lifecycle support rather than simply adding capability metadata.
families.shared_work: Repair task declarations and implementation together; do not declare unsupported task behavior.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies to tools declaring task support on a compatible revision.

rules.name: tools execution consistent
rules.easy_reason: Make task-support declarations match actual server task support.
rules.confidence_reason: The observed check is declarative; implementing the claimed feature can be substantial.

families.name: Tool inputs mapped to HTTP headers
families.easy_reason: Repair schema annotations and safely route eligible primitive inputs into headers.
families.confidence_reason: Most checks are structural, but sensitive-input handling may require interface changes.
families.shared_work: Review each x-mcp-header binding as a unit. Syntax, uniqueness, reachability and sensitivity are not interchangeable guarantees.
families.eligibility_note: Only for existing header mappings on the applicable revision; avoid adding this optional feature merely to gain points.

rules.name: tools mcp headers valid names
rules.easy_reason: Use valid HTTP header token names and update the matching binding.
rules.confidence_reason: The syntax check is explicit; integration must continue using the corrected name.

rules.name: tools mcp headers unique
rules.easy_reason: Remove case-insensitive duplicate header mappings within each tool.
rules.confidence_reason: Duplicate detection is straightforward; conflicting inputs may require a design decision.

rules.name: tools mcp headers primitive types
rules.easy_reason: Map supported string, integer or boolean inputs, or redesign unsupported bindings.
rules.confidence_reason: Changing array or object inputs may affect clients and serialization.

rules.name: tools mcp headers statically reachable
rules.easy_reason: Put mapped inputs on supported statically reachable property paths.
rules.confidence_reason: Schema composition and references can make this more than a field edit.

rules.name: tools mcp headers not sensitive
rules.easy_reason: Review sensitive mapped inputs and move credentials or personal data into appropriate protected mechanisms.
rules.confidence_reason: The detector is heuristic; renaming a sensitive field is not a substantive fix.

families.name: Prompt and argument identifiers
families.easy_reason: Repair prompt names and per-prompt argument names in the registry and handler mappings.
families.confidence_reason: Validation is simple, but identifier changes can affect callers.
families.shared_work: Validate prompt definitions before publishing them; top-level prompt and argument naming remain distinct requirements.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies to an existing or intended prompt feature.

rules.name: prompts argument names unique
rules.easy_reason: Give each argument a unique name within its own prompt and update handler lookups.
rules.confidence_reason: The uniqueness scope is explicit; renaming affects argument references.

rules.name: prompts argument names present
rules.easy_reason: Add nonblank names and valid argument records to existing prompts.
rules.confidence_reason: The field expectation is narrow, including malformed argument-list handling.

rules.name: prompts names unique
rules.easy_reason: Give published prompts distinct identifiers and update dispatch mappings.
rules.confidence_reason: The duplicate condition is direct; external callers may rely on existing names.

families.name: Prompt documentation
families.easy_reason: Add truthful descriptions to existing prompt and argument definitions.
families.confidence_reason: These checks test nonblank metadata, while useful descriptions require domain review.
families.shared_work: Edit the prompt-definition source once to cover prompt and argument descriptions; both fields still need content.
families.eligibility_note: Do not enable prompts or invent unused arguments solely to turn skipped checks into passes.

rules.name: prompts description present
rules.easy_reason: Add accurate descriptions to existing prompts.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator checks nonblank strings rather than content quality.

rules.name: prompts arguments documented
rules.easy_reason: Add accurate descriptions to the existing prompt arguments.
rules.confidence_reason: The required fields are explicit; malformed argument records also need repair.

families.name: Resource identifiers and names
families.easy_reason: Normalize resource identifiers and repair published names without breaking reads.
families.confidence_reason: Syntax and uniqueness are explicit; changing URIs can affect client references.
families.shared_work: Use a consistent resource registry for listing and reads. Identifier validity, uniqueness and display names remain separate fields.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies to existing or intended resources; URI syntax does not prove resource availability.

rules.name: resources uris valid
rules.easy_reason: Publish valid absolute resource URIs and keep read handlers aligned.
rules.confidence_reason: URI syntax is explicit, but correcting identifiers can require client migration.

rules.name: resources names present
rules.easy_reason: Add nonblank display names to existing resource entries.
rules.confidence_reason: This is a direct field-presence check with little structural ambiguity.

rules.name: resources uris unique
rules.easy_reason: Remove duplicate identifiers or assign distinct URIs to distinct resources.
rules.confidence_reason: Uniqueness is clear; deduplication must preserve intended resources and references.

families.name: Resource descriptions and metadata
families.easy_reason: Correct descriptions and supplied size, media-type and timestamp fields.
families.confidence_reason: Most checks are local metadata validation; actual resource content still needs verification.
families.shared_work: Repair resource-list serialization and its source metadata. Optional absent fields need no invented values.
families.eligibility_note: Only supplied optional fields should be repaired; do not fabricate size or modification timestamps.

rules.name: resources sizes valid
rules.easy_reason: Publish nonnegative integer sizes when size metadata is supplied.
rules.confidence_reason: The type check is clear; accurate byte counts depend on the content source.

rules.name: resources mime types valid
rules.easy_reason: Use a syntactically valid media type matching the actual resource content.
rules.confidence_reason: Syntax repair is small; identifying the true content type still needs care.

rules.name: resources annotations valid
rules.easy_reason: Format supplied lastModified values as valid timestamps from the real source.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator tests syntax; timezone and upstream-data quality can complicate repair.

rules.name: resources description present
rules.easy_reason: Add a truthful nonblank description to each existing resource.
rules.confidence_reason: The metadata requirement is explicit; content quality is not measured.

families.name: Resource template identifiers and names
families.easy_reason: Repair URI-template syntax, uniqueness and published names while preserving expansion behavior.
families.confidence_reason: Syntax is testable, but changing templates can affect routes and callers.
families.shared_work: Validate the template registry and corresponding read routes together; a valid template does not prove expansion or access works.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies when resource templates are an intended feature.

rules.name: resource templates uri templates valid
rules.easy_reason: Correct URI-template syntax while preserving the intended variables and route.
rules.confidence_reason: The parser check is direct; expansion and route compatibility are not tested.

rules.name: resource templates unique
rules.easy_reason: Deduplicate templates or use distinct patterns for distinct resources.
rules.confidence_reason: Identifier uniqueness is clear; routing overlap may still require design work.

rules.name: resource templates names present
rules.easy_reason: Add a nonblank name to each existing template entry.
rules.confidence_reason: This is a narrow field-presence check.

families.name: Resource template descriptions and metadata
families.easy_reason: Repair descriptions and supplied media-type or timestamp fields in existing templates.
families.confidence_reason: The checks are localized but do not establish that template-backed resources match the declarations.
families.shared_work: Update template metadata serialization; each description, media type and timestamp must be independently accurate.
families.eligibility_note: Do not create optional template fields solely for points.

rules.name: resource templates mime types valid
rules.easy_reason: Use a valid media-type declaration for the actual template-backed resources.
rules.confidence_reason: Syntax is straightforward; the underlying content contract must be known.

rules.name: resource templates annotations valid
rules.easy_reason: Correct supplied lastModified timestamps using meaningful source data.
rules.confidence_reason: Syntax is explicit, but template-wide timestamps may depend on dynamic data.

rules.name: resource templates description present
rules.easy_reason: Add a truthful nonblank description to each existing template.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator tests presence, not prose quality.

families.name: Consistent cache metadata
families.easy_reason: Align cache scope and lifetime metadata across relevant gateway and paginated responses.
families.confidence_reason: A shared response builder helps, but choosing a safe cache policy depends on data ownership.
families.shared_work: Use one cache-policy source for ttlMs and cacheScope, including paginated lists and declared Skills listings. Validate each path separately.
families.eligibility_note: Check protocol revision, pagination and feature applicability; never mark caller-specific data public to pass a check.

rules.name: pagination cache scope consistent
rules.easy_reason: Emit one valid consistent cacheScope across the applicable listing pages.
rules.confidence_reason: The observed consistency test is clear; actual privacy classification is untested.

rules.name: Cache metadata
rules.easy_reason: Add valid ttlMs and cacheScope metadata to applicable successful gateway results.
rules.confidence_reason: Serialization is small once the correct cache behavior has been determined.

rules.name: Skills list cache hints
rules.easy_reason: Return the required cache metadata with an existing modern Skills listing.
rules.confidence_reason: The hint validation is explicit, but Skills and modern support must already work.

families.name: Existing Skills listing and retrieval
families.easy_reason: Repair declared Skills routes, resource capability alignment and unknown-entry handling.
families.confidence_reason: Listing and retrieval may require SDK extensions and integration with a real Skills store.
families.shared_work: Connect Skills listing and retrieval to the same registry; declaring resources or adding error handling alone does not implement Skills.
families.eligibility_note: Only recommend repairs for a deliberately supported Skills feature, not for an undeclared optional extension.

rules.name: skills list supported
rules.easy_reason: Implement a usable skills/list response for the declared extension.
rules.confidence_reason: The returned array contract is clear; the SDK may lack native support.

rules.name: skills get supported
rules.easy_reason: Return a complete skill entry for each requested listed skill URI.
rules.confidence_reason: The check combines metadata, manifest, naming and requested-URI agreement.

rules.name: skills get unknown rejected
rules.easy_reason: Reject genuinely unknown skill requests with the required error response.
rules.confidence_reason: A focused handler change is likely once the existing lookup distinguishes unknown entries.

rules.name: skills resources capability
rules.easy_reason: Declare resources alongside Skills only when the resource handlers genuinely work.
rules.confidence_reason: The check is declarative; implementing missing resource behavior can be substantial.

families.name: Skill directory reads
families.easy_reason: Implement the declared directory-read contract, containment rules and missing/file-path rejection.
families.confidence_reason: This involves several filesystem or virtual-store behaviors and may require extension support.
families.shared_work: Use one contained directory resolver for listing and error cases; correct listing alone does not prove rejection paths.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies when directoryRead is intentionally declared; do not enable it just to gain points.

rules.name: skills directory read
rules.easy_reason: Return valid direct children including SKILL.md and reject file or unknown directory requests.
rules.confidence_reason: The tested contract spans listing, containment and negative cases, so effort depends on storage design.

families.name: Skill names and listing fields
families.easy_reason: Align skill listing fields, frontmatter names and directory identities.
families.confidence_reason: Most edits are metadata changes, but renaming directories can affect URIs and consumers.
families.shared_work: Generate listing identity from the actual skill package metadata and directory; each naming constraint remains independently checked.
families.eligibility_note: Requires existing listed skills and usable skill URIs.

rules.name: skills entries well formed
rules.easy_reason: Supply required URI, frontmatter name and bounded description fields for existing skills.
rules.confidence_reason: The listing-shape requirements are explicit; malformed packages may need broader repair.

rules.name: skills name matches uri
rules.easy_reason: Align the actual skill directory name with its frontmatter name.
rules.confidence_reason: The name comparison is explicit; URI changes can affect references and routing.

rules.name: skills name valid
rules.easy_reason: Use an allowed lowercase skill name and update dependent identities consistently.
rules.confidence_reason: Naming constraints are explicit; renaming can affect directory and manifest references.

families.name: Skill manifests and file integrity
families.easy_reason: Generate manifests, file sizes and digests from the same actual files and enforce the packaging limits.
families.confidence_reason: A build step can address several checks, but storage consistency and bounded reads affect observations.
families.shared_work: Rebuild static manifests from real bytes. Valid declarations, matching digests and size limits remain different requirements.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies to relevant existing skill manifests; incomplete reads should trigger evidence collection rather than invented integrity failures.

rules.name: skills resources manifest
rules.easy_reason: Generate a contained valid static manifest or truthfully declare a dynamic manifest.
rules.confidence_reason: Validation includes URI containment, uniqueness, sizes, digests and the skill entry itself.

rules.name: skills digest integrity
rules.easy_reason: Recompute declared sizes and SHA-256 digests from the exact bytes served.
rules.confidence_reason: The comparison is deterministic; stale storage or partial reads can complicate diagnosis.

rules.name: skills within limits
rules.easy_reason: Reduce or restructure static packages that exceed the evaluator file or byte limits.
rules.confidence_reason: Limits are explicit; splitting packages can change how consumers use them.

families.name: Skill source and reference consistency
families.easy_reason: Align listing frontmatter with actual SKILL.md content and repair local referenced paths.
families.confidence_reason: Build automation can help, but generated files, parser limits and package layout can differ.
families.shared_work: Generate listing metadata and manifests from the same skill source, then validate relative references; metadata agreement alone does not repair links.
families.eligibility_note: Unsupported YAML or unread source files should not be recast as simple metadata failures.

rules.name: skills frontmatter matches
rules.easy_reason: Keep the served SKILL.md frontmatter and listing frontmatter structurally equal.
rules.confidence_reason: Equality is explicit, but generation and YAML support can affect the observed result.

rules.name: skills references resolve
rules.easy_reason: Correct relative Markdown references to files actually included within the skill manifest.
rules.confidence_reason: The check uses local manifest resolution, while package layout and generated links vary.

families.name: Verified endpoint HTTPS
families.easy_reason: Configure a valid certificate and HTTPS termination for the assessed endpoint.
families.confidence_reason: Managed hosting can make this easy; custom proxies, certificate chains and DNS can take longer.
families.shared_work: Repair the endpoint certificate and TLS termination rather than disabling client verification.
families.eligibility_note: Requires control of the endpoint or its hosting configuration.

rules.name: Verified HTTPS/TLS
rules.easy_reason: Serve the endpoint through HTTPS with a certificate that passes normal verification.
rules.confidence_reason: Infrastructure ownership, certificate issuance and proxy setup determine effort.

families.name: Safe error details
families.easy_reason: Remove unintended sensitive error details while preserving useful diagnostics privately.
families.confidence_reason: The detector uses patterns rather than a complete diagnosis of what was exposed.
families.shared_work: Review the captured failing error and central exception handling. Redact actual exposure; do not merely evade a text pattern.
families.eligibility_note: Confirm the matched evidence and intended disclosure before changing responses.

rules.name: Error response exposure patterns
rules.easy_reason: Inspect the captured error and remove unintended sensitive or internal response details.
rules.confidence_reason: Pattern failure does not identify every leaked field or guarantee that one redaction is sufficient.

families.name: Foreign website request rejection
families.easy_reason: Validate Origin headers in the request middleware and use the revision-appropriate rejection behavior.
families.confidence_reason: The middleware change is usually focused; valid controls and proxy header handling still matter.
families.shared_work: Apply a deliberate Origin policy while preserving legitimate clients and same-Origin behavior.
families.eligibility_note: A missing successful control is an evidence issue, not proof the server accepts foreign Origins.

rules.name: Foreign Origin refused
rules.easy_reason: Reject disallowed foreign Origins using the applicable response contract.
rules.confidence_reason: The paired-control probe is specific, but reverse proxies and client requirements can complicate implementation.

families.name: Protected resource authentication metadata
families.easy_reason: Align an existing authentication challenge and resource metadata with the protected endpoint and issuer configuration.
families.confidence_reason: Many changes are metadata edits, but correct discovery depends on authentication architecture and endpoint ownership.
families.shared_work: Generate the challenge reference, protected-resource identity, issuer URLs and optional scopes from one configuration. Each check still needs its own valid response.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies to the established applicable authentication scheme; anonymous or non-Bearer service skips are not defects.

rules.name: Authentication challenge present
rules.easy_reason: Return the appropriate nonblank authentication challenge for an observed protected HTTP 401 response.
rules.confidence_reason: The field expectation is explicit; HTTP 403 alone does not require the same conclusion.

rules.name: Protected resource metadata identifies endpoint
rules.easy_reason: Serve discoverable resource metadata identifying the actual protected endpoint.
rules.confidence_reason: This may need a route plus correct deployment identity and issuer configuration.

rules.name: Advertised issuer URLs are valid HTTPS identifiers
rules.easy_reason: Correct advertised issuer URLs to valid HTTPS identifiers.
rules.confidence_reason: URL requirements are explicit, but the identifiers must match the actual authentication provider.

rules.name: Challenge metadata reference works
rules.easy_reason: Make an advertised challenge metadata reference resolve to usable resource metadata.
rules.confidence_reason: The reference path is clear; revision-specific mandatory-reference behavior and routing can differ.

rules.name: Authorization scopes advertised
rules.easy_reason: Advertise accurate nonempty scope strings when supplying the optional scopes field.
rules.confidence_reason: The check tests metadata shape; choosing real supported scopes needs authentication knowledge.

families.name: Verified metadata HTTPS
families.easy_reason: Repair certificate and redirect security on the actual authentication metadata hosts.
families.confidence_reason: Metadata may live on third-party infrastructure outside the MCP server owner control.
families.shared_work: Coordinate HTTPS and certificate fixes across the metadata-fetch chain; fixing the main MCP endpoint alone may not help.
families.eligibility_note: Only for observed applicable metadata fetches; identify who controls each failing host.

rules.name: Metadata fetched with verified HTTPS
rules.easy_reason: Ensure actual metadata fetches and redirects use verified HTTPS.
rules.confidence_reason: Multiple hosts and third-party certificate ownership make effort variable.

families.name: Authorization issuer discovery
families.easy_reason: Repair the existing issuer discovery document and truthful capability declarations.
families.confidence_reason: An external identity provider may control these values; changing metadata alone does not implement authentication features.
families.shared_work: Use the actual issuer configuration for exact identity, HTTPS endpoints and supported PKCE methods.
families.eligibility_note: Requires an applicable established OAuth flow and access to the identity-provider configuration.

rules.name: Issuer discovery metadata usable
rules.easy_reason: Publish matching issuer identity and valid HTTPS authorization and token endpoints.
rules.confidence_reason: Document structure is clear, but provider ownership and deployment routing may limit control.

rules.name: Issuer advertises PKCE S256
rules.easy_reason: Advertise S256 only after the issuer genuinely supports that PKCE method.
rules.confidence_reason: The evaluator checks advertisement and does not establish runtime enforcement or upgrade effort.

families.name: Invalid token rejection
families.easy_reason: Repair authentication enforcement on the same protected discovery route without relying on a misleading success wrapper.
families.confidence_reason: The collection can establish some failures, but complete token validation depends on the provider and middleware.
families.shared_work: Check the authentication gate and token verification before dispatching protected discovery.
families.eligibility_note: Only for a clearly established applicable authentication gate with conclusive evidence.

rules.name: Fabricated token denied protected discovery
rules.easy_reason: Prevent a fabricated token from obtaining previously protected protocol discovery.
rules.confidence_reason: Repair may require authentication middleware changes; generic success responses can be inconclusive.

families.name: Catalog text safety review
families.easy_reason: Review flagged catalog text and remove unintended hidden text, credentials or instruction-like content.
families.confidence_reason: These are bounded heuristic scans with different causes and possible false positives.
families.shared_work: Review the actual affected catalog entries together; one text edit may help multiple patterns but has no guaranteed joint effect.
families.eligibility_note: Check the exact evidence and intended content; rotate real exposed secrets where needed rather than just removing visible strings.

rules.name: Catalog hidden Unicode patterns
rules.easy_reason: Inspect flagged hidden characters and remove unintended content while preserving legitimate language.
rules.confidence_reason: The scan is pattern-based, and some characters can be intentional.

rules.name: Catalog credential patterns
rules.easy_reason: Remove real credentials from catalog content and rotate or revoke any exposed secret as appropriate.
rules.confidence_reason: Exposure response may extend beyond a metadata edit; the pattern match alone is not proof of a real secret.

rules.name: Catalog injection phrasing
rules.easy_reason: Review flagged instructions and remove unintended attempts to redirect consumers.
rules.confidence_reason: A phrase pattern needs semantic review and can match legitimate examples.

families.name: Skill text safety review
families.easy_reason: Review flagged skill descriptions and served files, then repair the actual unsafe content and regenerated package metadata.
families.confidence_reason: The scan is bounded and heuristic; file changes may also require manifest and digest updates.
families.shared_work: Repair the affected skill source and rebuild its package; hidden text, credentials and instruction patterns remain independent findings.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies to collected applicable Skills content; absence of scan findings is not comprehensive safety evidence.

rules.name: Skills hidden Unicode patterns
rules.easy_reason: Remove unintended hidden characters from affected skill metadata or files.
rules.confidence_reason: Pattern interpretation needs review, and file edits may require digest regeneration.

rules.name: Skills credential patterns
rules.easy_reason: Remove actual secrets from skill content and handle rotation or revocation where necessary.
rules.confidence_reason: Secret remediation can affect external systems, while pattern matches may be false positives.

rules.name: Skills injection phrasing
rules.easy_reason: Remove unintended instruction attacks from the actual affected skill content.
rules.confidence_reason: Skill instructions need contextual review; naive phrase deletion can break legitimate documentation.

families.name: Modern server discovery
families.easy_reason: Implement the applicable discovery route with usable capabilities and target-version support.
families.confidence_reason: An SDK upgrade may provide the route; otherwise this introduces new protocol behavior.
families.shared_work: Expose discovery from the actual server registry; truthful capabilities and supported revisions must already be implemented.
families.eligibility_note: Do not fabricate modern capabilities or treat all legacy-only servers as a trivial metadata fix.

rules.name: Server discover
rules.easy_reason: Implement a usable server/discover response supporting the assessed target revision.
rules.confidence_reason: The required shape is explicit, but the server may need a protocol or SDK upgrade.

families.name: Modern stateless request handling
families.easy_reason: Support applicable listing without initialization or session state and avoid creating modern session IDs.
families.confidence_reason: This can require architectural changes for a server designed around legacy sessions.
families.shared_work: Review the modern request lifecycle and session middleware together; usable stateless listing and spurious-session handling are separate paths.
families.eligibility_note: Only when the modern behavior is supported or deliberately being implemented; preserve legitimate legacy contracts.

rules.name: Stateless request
rules.easy_reason: Serve usable applicable catalogs without prior initialization or session headers.
rules.confidence_reason: Removing a session dependency may require significant framework integration.

rules.name: No session id
rules.easy_reason: Ignore a spurious modern session ID and avoid minting or echoing one on the tested list response.
rules.confidence_reason: Often middleware configuration, but shared legacy session logic can complicate separation.

families.name: Modern header and metadata validation
families.easy_reason: Validate applicable request metadata and header agreement in shared middleware, with the required condition-specific errors.
families.confidence_reason: The probes have explicit expectations; several independent request conditions still need implementation.
families.shared_work: Implement shared request validation for metadata, version, method and supported name bindings. One response-code edit does not implement all validators.
families.eligibility_note: Respect the assessed revision, declared prompt/resource features and permitted legacy fallback. Zero-weight checks are informational.

rules.name: Meta validation
rules.easy_reason: Validate required request metadata and return the tested JSON-RPC error and HTTP status.
rules.confidence_reason: The expected negative case is clear; correct validation needs more than changing an error string.

rules.name: Header validation
rules.easy_reason: Validate request/header method agreement and produce the expected rejection response.
rules.confidence_reason: Shared middleware can help; routing and body/header parsing may need coordination.

rules.name: Missing protocol version rejected
rules.easy_reason: Reject a missing version header only when the applicable contract requires it.
rules.confidence_reason: Legacy handshake fallback can legitimately skip this zero-weight check.

rules.name: Missing method header rejected
rules.easy_reason: Reject missing method headers in the applicable modern request path.
rules.confidence_reason: The negative case is narrow and has explicit expected responses; the rule has zero weight.

rules.name: Resource name header mismatch rejected
rules.easy_reason: Compare the resource name header with the actual resource request target and reject mismatches.
rules.confidence_reason: Resource-specific dispatch and encoded identifiers can complicate a shared validator.

rules.name: Prompt name header mismatch rejected
rules.easy_reason: Compare the prompt name header with the requested prompt and reject mismatches.
rules.confidence_reason: The condition is explicit but requires an applicable prompt path and aligned routing.

families.name: Modern result and content-type metadata
families.easy_reason: Use the shared response builder to emit the correct completion marker and HTTP content type.
families.confidence_reason: These are focused serialization changes when the applicable gateway responses already work.
families.shared_work: Apply the response contract to both successful discovery and listing results; completion markers and content-type headers are distinct fields.
families.eligibility_note: Only applies to established modern successful gateway responses; do not label partial results complete.

rules.name: Result type
rules.easy_reason: Mark actually complete applicable gateway results with the required completion value.
rules.confidence_reason: The field condition is explicit; verify the underlying result really is complete.

rules.name: Response content type
rules.easy_reason: Set the correct JSON or SSE content type on applicable gateway responses.
rules.confidence_reason: Usually a localized response-header correction, unless proxies overwrite headers.

families.name: Tool schema dialect declaration
families.easy_reason: Align declared schema dialect metadata with the schemas actually served.
families.confidence_reason: The metadata change may be small, but some schemas need migration to the expected dialect.
families.shared_work: Review schema-generation configuration and the observed declaration together.
families.eligibility_note: Use the actual negotiated revision and observed tool schema evidence.

rules.name: Tool schema dialect
rules.easy_reason: Correct the observed tool schema dialect declaration or migrate incompatible schemas where required.
rules.confidence_reason: The expected dialect is checkable; schema compatibility determines the actual effort.
